text: what must happen when something this code calls (a helper, a host function, a callback) throws or rejects
what must happen when this code is given invalid, malformed or unexpected input
how an error from a dependency is told apart from a legitimate negative or empty answer
what state must be left behind when an operation fails partway through
how in-memory state must relate to what was actually written or sent, when the write or send fails
a limit on the size or length of values that come from outside (files, responses, user text)
that values received from outside must be checked field by field before use
how secrets or credentials must be kept out of logs, results and error text
what must happen when two operations run at the same time
a time limit or deadline, and what happens when it passes
which code must call each exported helper or guard, so that none is left unused
every closed list of allowed values, and what happens to a value outside the list
that failure paths, and not only the happy path, must have tests
how to turn the feature off or return to the old behaviour
a definition of each new term it introduces, precise enough to decide a borderline case
at least one worked borderline example showing which side of a new rule a near-miss case falls on
which single document owns each new rule, and that every other mention points at it or copies it whole
how two copies of the same text are kept identical (a pin, a build step or a test)
which existing sentences elsewhere contradict the new rule and must be changed or removed
for each new instruction, how the person following it can observe the condition that triggers it
how the new rule ranks against an existing rule it could collide with
what happens to existing items (tests, documents, records) that do not meet the new rule
acceptance points that a third party could check as true or false without judgment
that every file, section or name the new text refers to exists, and how that is checked
that comments and headers touched by the change must describe what the code actually does
the exact list of files each section may change
for each new rule with several outcomes, that every possible case gets exactly one outcome, with none left unassigned and none given two
for each test or check the change adds or edits, what it must select and what it must not select, and the control that proves it
